request.system: Assess whether the hypothesis or expression uses or tests numbered claims. Return JSON only: {"uses_claim": true|false, "claim_ids": []}.
request.prompt: {"claims": {"1": "**Migration report**", "2": "Four composition-style features were tried, all valid.", "3": "None was statistically convincing.", "4": "The most promising was the smoothed cross-sectional contrast between average hours and hourly wage.", "5": "Its mean IC was 0.03 (HAC t of 1.0), somewhat stronger in the high-T regime.", "6": "That is suggestive but not significant.", "7": "The clearest failure was the high-T-only flow-rate contrast.", "8": "It had an IC of -0.07 (t of -1.25), the opposite sign to my hypothesis, and coverage fell to 0.82.", "9": "The stock-versus-flow contrast and the wage-versus-turnover contrast both had ICs near zero.", "10": "Smoothed features have rank autocorrelation of 0.97 to 1.0, so their effective sample is small.", "11": "Base correlations were low, at most 0.18."}, "hypothesis": "Groups with a high V06 stock rate whose average hours V01 are rising over 6 months show early recovery from slack, so the interaction of their cross-sectional ranks predicts higher next-month returns; sign is positive.", "expression": "mult(csrank(V06),csrank(chg(V01,6)))"}
